evals.prompt: Add a sensor that exposes the device's current power draw in watts.
evals.expected_output: Creates a SensorEntityDescription with translation_key, SensorDeviceClass.POWER and SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT, reads the value from coordinator.data, and adds the translation key to en.json.
assertions: Uses translation_key in the EntityDescription rather than a hardcoded name=
Reads the value from coordinator.data instead of calling the API client from the entity
Does NOT set _attr_unique_id or _attr_device_info in the platform entity — the base entity owns those

evals.prompt: Add a sensor showing how long the last API request took. It is only interesting when something is broken.
evals.expected_output: Creates the sensor with entity_category=EntityCategory.DIAGNOSTIC and entity_registry_enabled_default=False.
assertions: Suggests entity_registry_enabled_default=False because the entity is rarely useful
Uses a duration device class or an explicit unit rather than a bare number

evals.prompt: Add a switch that turns the device's eco mode on and off.
evals.expected_output: Creates a switch whose class inherits (SwitchEntity, {ClassPrefix}Entity), calls the API client through runtime_data and requests a coordinator refresh after writing.
assertions: Declares the class as (SwitchEntity, <base entity>) with the Home Assistant platform base first
Calls async_request_refresh (or equivalent) after the write instead of only mutating local state
Wraps API failures in HomeAssistantError with a translation_key rather than letting a raw client error escape
